exposure: Precesarean internal iliac artery balloon catheterization
outcome: Intraoperative red blood cell transfusion volume
cohort: 128 women with suspected placenta accreta spectrum disorder (PASD) and placenta previa (PP) who had a history of cesarean section.
finding: Precesarean internal iliac artery balloon catheterization significantly reduced intraoperative blood loss, intraoperative red blood cell transfusions, and the incidence of hysterectomy compared to conventional cesarean delivery in women with PASD and PP.
followup_time: Up to 7 days postpartum (based on postoperation hospitalization)
